To the perpetually scorching "Ocean World (Planet No. 503)," Octavia wasn't the only newcomer on the beach — she had also brought along with her a yellow, oval, and lip-puckering fruit known as the lemon. Truth be told, Octavia wasn't a fan of lemons at all, and even found them a little off-putting. But nevertheless, she begrudgingly brought some along with her for her long voyage as a means to stave off potential illnesses.
By the time she arrived on Planet No. 503 after an arduous journey across five hundred planet, Octavia had completely forgotten about the lemons in her pack. But when she tried to order a salted lemon fizz at an Ocean World eatery, she discovered that the locals had no clue what a lemon even was, since the fruit only grows in temperate climates. In that moment, her memories came rushing back. As it turned out, a frosty salted lemon fizz was the perfect cure for the scorching heat, and when the locals pleaded with her, Octavia was happy to give away all her lemons so they could plant and grow their own. But since she had no interest in playing the divine, she firmly rejected the grand title of "Lemon Queen" they tried to confer on her. Instead, she took only this cool outfit gifted by the residents as a fond memento of this extraplanetary encounter.

To the perpetually scorching "Ocean World (Planet No. 503)," Octavia wasn't the only newcomer on the beach — she had also brought along with her a yellow, oval, and lip-puckering fruit known as the lemon. Truth be told, Octavia wasn't a fan of lemons at all, and even found them a little off-putting. But nevertheless, she begrudgingly brought some along with her for her long voyage as a means to stave off potential illnesses.
By the time she arrived on Planet No. 503 after an arduous journey across five hundred planets, Octavia had completely forgotten about the lemons in her pack. But when she tried to order a salted lemon fizz at an Ocean World eatery, she discovered that the locals had no clue what a lemon even was, since the fruit only grows in temperate climates. In that moment, her memories came rushing back. As it turned out, a frosty salted lemon fizz was the perfect cure for the scorching heat, and when the locals pleaded with her, Octavia was happy to give away all her lemons so they could plant and grow their own. But since she had no interest in playing the divine, she firmly rejected the grand title of "Lemon Queen" they tried to confer on her. Instead, she took only this cool outfit gifted by the residents as a fond memento of this extraplanetary encounter.

Early in her travels, Octavia arrived at Planet #31, which looked barren from above, though "parts of its surface bore the marks of human work." After landing, she discovered a civilization with widespread mastery of combustion engineering. What set them apart was that they lived clustered, nearly obsessively, in a hundred cities, combining giant canvases and living plants to "raise umbrellas" over every building, trying to disguise each city as a forest or a stretch of empty hills...

This strange phenomenon traced back to a single astronomer's warning. With a simple but effective telescope, he had captured the process of many stars being devoured by an "unnameable pitch-blackness," compiled his evidence in painstaking detail, and then spent thirty years lobbying every faction he could reach, convincing them all to undertake this civilization-scale act of disguise.

"Fighting a thing like that is a fool's hope. We have to hide, buy ourselves time, lay down a technological foundation firm enough to matter..."

As the astronomer's own children, a pair of young siblings were shaped from infancy by the terrors beyond the sky, dreaming they might one day solve the problem for good. And then a phantom thief's illusion show gave them the direction they'd throw everything into...

Thus, they mounted the second grand illusion show, unprecedented then and never quite matched since. Their command of the art was all but flawless. Whimsical Spectacle Set. Master illusionists bent on "deceiving the very stars" once wore these formal costumes onto the most exalted stages, with gravitas and grace as much a part of the act as anything else.

Early in her travels, Octavia arrived at Planet #31, which looked barren from above, though "parts of its surface bore the marks of human work." After landing, she discovered a civilization with widespread mastery of combustion engineering. What set them apart was that they lived clustered, nearly obsessively, in a hundred cities, combining giant canvases and living plants to "raise umbrellas" over every building, trying to disguise each city as a forest or a stretch of empty hills...

This strange phenomenon traced back to a single astronomer's warning. With a simple but effective telescope, he had captured the process of many stars being devoured by an "unnameable pitch-blackness," compiled his evidence in painstaking detail, and then spent thirty years lobbying every faction he could reach, convincing them all to undertake this civilization-scale act of disguise.

"Fighting a thing like that is a fool's hope. We have to hide, buy ourselves time, lay down a technological foundation firm enough to matter..."

As the astronomer's own children, a pair of young siblings were shaped from infancy by the terrors beyond the sky, dreaming they might one day solve the problem for good. And then a phantom thief's illusion show gave them the direction they'd throw everything into...
